title: Indoor Single-Wall Mirror Reflection
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a simple room with one mirrored wall: you may use three/addons/objects/Reflector.js or manually implement planar reflection with a renderTarget.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
import { Reflector } from 'three/addons/objects/Reflector.js';
</script>

[Scene]
(1) Room: a floor and four walls, or one side left open for the camera; one entire wall, or most of it, must be a mirror.
(2) Place 5 objects of different shapes and colors in the room, distributed across different positions (for example, one each of a box, sphere, cone, cylinder, and torus).

[Interaction]
(3) A slider with id="reflectivity" and range 0–1 controls the mirror reflection intensity or a Reflector-related parameter (the implementation must be consistent with __3D_STATE__.mirrorReflectivity).
(4) Object color: a dropdown or color picker with id="objectColorSelect" changes the currently selected object's color or applies a uniform color adjustment (this must be reflected in __3D_STATE__.objects[].color as a hex string such as '#ff00aa').
(5) Mirror tint: a color input with id="mirrorTint" (or color + text) maps to the mirror's color filtering.

[State Exposure (Required)]
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame:
  - mirrorReflectivity: number (0–1)
  - mirrorTint: string (for example, '#ffffff')
  - objectCount: number (5)
  - objects: Array<{ name: string, x: number, y: number, z: number, color: string }>
  - fps: number

Output a single HTML file.
